reasoning: The document has a low fidelity composite score of 0.6967 and exhibits multiple critical and major structural defects that strictly block auto-approval. Notably, all 8 hyperlinks from the source PDF were lost during extraction, images are placed out of sequence, list numbering restarts incorrectly, heading hierarchy is broken, and header/footer elements were retained. These pervasive structural and content issues require human intervention.

concerns.description: Source PDF has 8 hyperlinks but output has none — all links lost during extraction
concerns.analysis: source_link_count=8, output_link_count=0. PDF URI annotations were not preserved as link elements.

Checked heading levels across the document. On page 2, there are three column headers ('How to reset your password', 'How to change your password', and 'How to update your profile') which share the exact same visual hierarchy and style in the source. However, in the output, the first is assigned as an H2, while the other two are improperly nested as H3s.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Visually equivalent column headers: "How to reset your password", "How to change your password", and "How to update your profile"
concerns.output_quote: {"type": "heading", "level": 2, "text": "How to reset your password"} followed by {"type": "heading", "level": 3, "text": "How to change your password"}

concerns.description: Images placed next to wrong text
concerns.analysis: The extraction process has grouped and misplaced several images out of their correct sequence. In the 'How to reset your password' section, an image illustrating steps 4 and 6 is placed incorrectly after step 2.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 2, 'How to reset your password', Step 2 instructs the user to click 'Trouble Signing On?' and is followed by an image of that specific link.
concerns.output_quote: Immediately after Step 2, the HTML places an image with the alt text 'A set of instructions for resetting an account password, featuring screenshots of the "Forgot Password" link and a blue "Submit" button...'. This image is placed next to the wrong instructional text.
concerns.location: Page 2, 'How to reset your password' section

concerns.description: Header/footer elements retained in output (3): MyNCID User Guide * Ver 1.0; September 23, 2025; Page 1 of 3
concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=3. Running headers/footers/page numbers should be stripped during PDF-to-HTML conversion.

concerns.description: List numbering restart(s): 1 ordered list(s) restart numbering at 1 instead of continuing sequence
concerns.analysis: restart_count=1. Examples: p3: 2 single-item ordered lists (fragmented). Ordered lists that restart numbering suggest content was split across page breaks and not reassembled.

Continuous numbered lists in the source document are broken into multiple separate 'ordered list' objects whenever interrupted by an image. Because there is no 'start' attribute defining the continuation of the numbering in the JSON, each new list block functionally resets to 1. For example, in the 'How to register' section, item 6 is rendered as the first item of a brand new list.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: 6. Go to your email and click on the activation link to complete the registration.
concerns.output_quote: {"type": "list", "list_type": "ordered", "items": [{"text": "Go to your email and click on the activation link to complete the registration."}]}

concerns.analysis: Several meaningful inline images (such as buttons) are missing or incorrectly captured in the HTML. For instance, the image of the 'SAVE' button in the 'How to update your profile' section is entirely absent from the output, having been replaced by an image of the page footer.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: Page 2, 'How to update your profile', Step 4 includes an inline image of a teal 'SAVE' button.
concerns.output_quote: The image element following Step 4 contains the alt text: 'The image shows a plain white background with a vertical dark blue line on the left side and the text "Page 2 of 3" located in the bottom right corner.' The SAVE button image is missing.
